# Use Azure DevOps Repos for branches and pull requests

For a project owner. Procedure `connector.scm.azure-repos`, version 1, reviewed 2026-11-20 against the vendor's own pages.

## Before you start

- An Azure DevOps organisation (Azure DevOps Services) or an Azure DevOps Server 2022 collection, a Git
  repository the agents change, and an account **dedicated to Tranibor**.
- **Two credentials, not one.** The connector's own (`pat`, or a service principal) reads and writes pull
  requests and stays on the platform. Azure DevOps cannot make a short-lived, repository-scoped credential,
  so the platform makes none: **a run is given `run_token`, or nothing**. Create a second personal access
  token, for a second account if you can, scoped to **Code: Read & write** only. Without `run_token`, runs
  cannot clone or push, and the connector says why.
- The platform's shared webhook secret (`TRANIBOR_GENERIC_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), held by whoever operates
  Tranibor, if you want pull request events. A service hook does not sign its deliveries.

## At Azure DevOps

1. **The credential.** A personal access token of the dedicated account (works on the Services and on
   Server), scopes **Code: Read & write**, **Code: Status**, **Build: Read** and **Project and Team: Read**.
   Or, on the Services only, a Microsoft Entra service principal added to the organisation and to the
   project's Contributors.
2. **The run token.** A second personal access token, scope **Code: Read & write** only.
3. **Branch policies on the target branch** (Repos, Branches, the branch's **Branch policies**): add a
   **Build validation** policy for your pipeline. This is where the pull request's checks come from: the
   platform reads the Build and Status policies of the pull request, and Azure refuses to complete it while
   they are not met. Tranibor never bypasses a policy and never sets auto-complete.
4. **Service hooks** (optional). **Project settings**, **Service hooks**, **Create subscription**, **Web
   Hooks**: one each for **Pull request created** and **Pull request updated**. URL:
   `<api_url>/api/v1/webhooks/azure-devops`; basic authentication password: the platform's shared webhook
   secret. This path has not been exercised against a live organisation from this repository.

## Permissions

On the repository, for the dedicated account: **Read**, **Contribute**, **Create branch**, **Contribute to
pull requests**. **Bypass policies when completing pull requests** must be left denied. A reviewer is
asked by sign-in name or e-mail, resolved through the organisation's identities.

**What a merge means here.** The platform completes the pull request at the commit its guarantees judged
(`lastMergeSourceCommit`): if someone pushed meanwhile, nothing is completed and the work item is judged
again. Completion is asynchronous on Azure's side; the platform waits a few seconds and, if it is still
queued, a replay finds it done.

## In Tranibor

1. Project settings, Connectors, **SCM**, type **Azure DevOps Repos**.
2. `base_url`, `project`, `repository`, `default_branch`, and `merge_strategy` if your repository forbids
   squash. `auth`: `pat` (the default) or `entra`, with `tenant_id` and `client_id`.
3. `pat` (or `client_secret`) and `run_token`: in the password fields (sealed, shown once).
4. The pull request's CI is read from its Build policy and from the builds of its branch; add a **CI**
   connector of type **Azure Pipelines** on the same team project to queue runs and read their logs.

## Test it

Press **Test**: the connector reads the repository and answers `ok` with its default branch. Then start a
run: a branch is pushed with the run token, a pull request opens, and its checks appear once the Build
policy has queued the pipeline.

## When it fails

- `401` or a sign-in page (`203`): a wrong, expired or revoked token, or a service principal that is not a
  member of the organisation.
- `403` on the pull request: the account lacks **Contribute to pull requests**; on a push, **Contribute**.
- `404` on the repository: wrong `project` or `repository`, or the account is not in the project.
- `scm/azure-repos mints no token`: set `run_token` on the connector.
- Completion refused with a policy message: a branch policy is not met yet (a required build, a minimum
  number of reviewers). The platform does not bypass it; the gates wait or fail as for any other forge.
- A build with warnings (`partiallySucceeded`) holds the gates back: that is the default. Set
  `partially_succeeded: neutral` only if your pipelines use warnings for things that are not failures.
- A timeout: the egress allowlist must open `dev.azure.com` (or your Server), `vssps.dev.azure.com` and, for
  a service principal, `login.microsoftonline.com`.

## Fields

| Field | What to put in it |
| :-- | :-- |
| `auth` | `pat` (the default) for a personal access token; `entra` for a Microsoft Entra service principal, Azure DevOps Services only |
| `base_url` | https://dev.azure.com/<organisation>, or the collection of an Azure DevOps Server 2022 (https://<server>/<path>/<collection>) |
| `client_id` | `entra` only: the service principal's application (client) id |
| `client_secret` | the service principal's client secret, typed once (`auth: entra`) |
| `default_branch` | the branch pull requests target (default `main`) |
| `delete_source_branch` | delete the work branch when the pull request is completed (default off) |
| `merge_strategy` | how a pull request is completed: `squash` (the default), `noFastForward`, `rebase` or `rebaseMerge` |
| `partially_succeeded` | how a build that partially succeeded counts for the gates: `failure` (the default) or `neutral` |
| `pat` | the connector's personal access token, typed once (`auth: pat`) |
| `project` | the Azure DevOps team project |
| `repository` | the Azure Repos Git repository, by name or id |
| `run_token` | a second, narrower personal access token that runs clone and push with, typed once |
| `tenant_id` | `entra` only: the Entra tenant (directory) id |

## Network egress

Hosts the platform must be allowed to reach:

- `dev.azure.com, or your Azure DevOps Server host`
- `vssps.dev.azure.com (reviewers are looked up there)`
- `login.microsoftonline.com (service principal)`
